results.description:
Troops Repel Terrorist Attack Along Sokoto–Gusau Road, Killed Several bandits, 
Rescue Civilian

By: Zagazola Makama

Troops of the Nigerian Army have killed several bandits and rescued civilians after it’s repelled an attack by suspected terrorists around Kuka Mairaho Village, along the Sokoto–Gusau Main Supply Route (MSR). 

Security sources said the incident occurred at about 11:15 a.m. on November 1, 2026, when troops deployed at Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) Fangaltama and Gidan Kano were alerted to sounds of gunshots around the village.

The sources said the troops immediately mobilised to the location and engaged the terrorists, killing several fighters and forcing others  to withdraw in disarray.

Following the engagement, the troops exploited the general area and rescued one civilian.
The rescued victim is currently in military custody for further action.

Troops continue to maintain security along the Sokoto–Gusau road and surrounding communities.

results.description:
Security operatives repel bandit attacks in Kebbi, one killed

The Kebbi State Police Command has confirmed that joint security operatives repelled two successive attacks by suspected bandits on Ribah community in Zuru Local Government Area.

One person was killed during the incidents.

Police spokesperson SP Bashir Usman said the attackers first attempted to block Rambo Junction along the Ribah–Dirin Daji Road at about 7:25pm on Friday before security operatives swiftly confronted them.

#GbaramatuVoice

results.title: No precise official tally exists for civilian or total deaths from banditry/insurgency (including Lakurawa groups) in Sokoto over the past s
results.description: No precise official tally exists for civilian or total deaths from banditry/insurgency (including Lakurawa groups) in Sokoto over the past six months. Media reports document dozens of attacks with cumulative fatalities well into the scores—for example, over 77 from late June to early August, 21 in one August Sabon Birni raid, plus further incidents through October—though numbers remain incomplete and unconsolidated.

results.title: An image circulating on Facebook claims that bandits abducted 40 students and killed the vice principal of a Government Girls Secondary Scho
results.description:
An image circulating on Facebook claims that bandits abducted 40 students and killed the vice principal of a Government Girls Secondary School in Zamfara State.

Verdict: False.

DUBAWA found that the image was originally linked to a school abduction in Maga, Kebbi State, involving 25 students. It does not show a recent abduction of 40 students in Zamfara State.

#CounteringDisinformation #EmpoweringDemocracy #DUBAWAChecks #MediaLiteracy

results.title: 🚨 NIGERIA IS LOSING THE VERY PEOPLE TASKED WITH PROTECTING IT.
results.description:
🚨 NIGERIA IS LOSING THE VERY PEOPLE TASKED WITH PROTECTING IT.

Bandits have reportedly killed Nigerian police officers travelling from Sokoto to Zamfara for a special assignment.

These officers left to serve and protect, but never made it to their destination.

How many more lives must be lost before the security situation receives the urgent attention it deserves?

Nigeria cannot afford to keep burying its defenders.

May their souls rest in peace. 🇳🇬
